intent: Did we diagnose the Q3 revenue contraction correctly, or are we pattern-matching the checkout regression?

user_turns.text: Revenue is down 5.5% MoM. We think it's the checkout regression — but I'm not 100% sure.
The question I'm actually asking: is the regression THE cause, or just A cause?
Checkout conversion dropped from 92% to 71% the week after the SDK upgrade. Other funnels look normal.
But session count is also down ~12% — and that started two weeks BEFORE the SDK upgrade.
So we're conflating two things: a session-acquisition decline AND a conversion regression.
If both signals are real, the recovery plan needs to address both — not just checkout.
We assumed checkout because it was loud. The session decline was quiet but earlier.

synthesis.body:
## Diagnosis

Two independent causes underlie the Q3 contraction. The checkout regression cleanly maps to a conversion drop the week of the SDK upgrade. The session-acquisition decline started two weeks earlier and is independent of the SDK story.

The original framing ('the funnel is broken') would have shipped a single-cause recovery plan. The sharpened framing ('which of these two signals is dominant?') changes the question the recovery plan must answer.

## Stop-at-diagnosis

Seek Clarity stops here. Develop Strategy would answer 'what's the sequenced recovery pathway given two causes?' — that is a separate call against a separate path.

recommendations.heading: Pressure-test sector benchmark before committing the recovery plan
recommendations.body: Whether session softness is sector-driven could be tested by pulling comparable-cohort weekly index data over the same period.

recommendations.heading: Watch session recovery independence
recommendations.body: If sessions recover on their own as the SDK fix ships, the two-cause read would be falsified — checkout was the only cause.
